caption:
Pi updates can break your extensions.
This system maintains those add-ons for you.
say: Pie updates can break your extensions. This system maintains those add-ons for you.
source: main README purpose; Pi defined in picture as coding assistant

caption:
Two lead agents assign work to delegates:
specialists who fix or review an extension.
source: FLOW Nodes; main agents make their own forks

caption:
Fixer delegates edit their extension’s copy.
Reviewer delegates check the work.
source: FLOW Powers 1–3; persistent clones

caption:
Reviewers approve or reject code changes.
They also judge questions for you.
source: FLOW Powers 2; patch defined visually as code changes; main reviewer passes unchanged

caption:
The main fixer chooses what happens next:
release, return or hold.
source: FLOW fix gate; terms pictured as publish, rework, wait

caption:
Release moves approved work forward.
Product changes still need your separate push tap.
source: FLOW Powers 6; same reviewed files and base; product defined visually as changed user behavior

caption:
A return sends work back for revision.
The next review sees the reasons too.
source: FLOW findings list; original reviewer text retained in order

caption:
After three returns, both delegates write
handoffs: notes for their replacements.
source: FLOW limit; hold costs no return

caption:
A hold waits for a named answer.
The main fixer can ask you directly.
source: FLOW hold and direct ask; cross-extension concern pictured

caption:
Telegram asks one question at a time.
Your answer is handled before the next.
source: FLOW Answers; PROTOCOL-FIXES D5

caption:
Late answers reach the current main fixer.
A retired delegate is replaced, with notes.
source: FLOW Answers 4–7; partial answer shown in bubble; private context note

caption:
A run groups maintenance work. Usage limits
pause it without replacing the agents.
source: FLOW runs, lifetimes and quota; fresh run pictured separately

caption:
Programs restart when work arrives.
Saved conversations preserve the agents’ memory.
source: DECISIONS event-scoped RPC processes; normal restart, not crash recovery

caption:
The first trial must discard two old patches.
Pi 1.4 already fixes their problem.
say: The first trial must discard two old patches. Pie one point four already fixes their problem.
source: design README acceptance test 1

caption:
The team extension still helps Pi 1.3 users.
Removing that extra fix needs your choice.
say: The team extension still helps Pie one point three users. Removing that extra fix needs your choice.
source: design README acceptance test 2

caption:
The first version is built, but switched off.
Automatic crash recovery comes later.
source: main README status; FLOW Recovery; later automatic default answers explained in art

caption:
Bend checks design rules, called laws,
against a simplified model of the system.
source: lock README scope; introduced model, laws and Bend in words and picture

caption:
Its 52 checks cover the model, not the code.
You still need to approve those rules.
say: Its fifty two checks cover the model, not the code. You still need to approve those rules.
source: Bend scope; REVIEWS law approval and connecting model to Python remain open

caption:
First choice: two items go back to one delegate.
Does that spend one return, or two?
source: LOCK-DIFF Q1; no policy chosen

caption:
Counting once saves a retry for the delegate.
The build counts each item separately.
source: LOCK-DIFF Q1; 0→1 versus 0→2 shown as remaining allowance

caption:
Second choice: the system refuses
a forbidden action. What happens next?
source: LOCK-DIFF Q2; return to retired delegate is invalid

caption:
The build pauses, notifies you, then retries.
You have not approved that failure policy.
source: LOCK-DIFF Q2; next scheduled check retries same run; clone edits stay

caption:
Third choice: GitHub changes after a review.
Pushing the old patch is blocked.
source: LOCK-DIFF Q3; moved reviewed base blocks publication

caption:
The build updates the copy before retrying.
A new product patch needs another review and tap.
source: LOCK-DIFF Q3; current build follow-up remains open policy

caption:
Fourth choice: withdrawing a held question
can leave it able to reappear. How should it close?
source: LOCK-DIFF Q4b: resolved Ask plus held Item can reopen; obsolete answer pictured

caption:
Dropping could close any obsolete item.
Wider withdrawal could close unreleased questions.
source: lock README Q4 proposals; no selection; questions-only limit of wider withdrawal shown

caption:
Or close old held items when a new run starts.
New delegates would reconsider the work.
source: lock README Q4 run-start closing option; REVIEWS describes old holds as new input

caption:
Choose the policies and review the rules.
Then decide whether to start the live trial.
source: LOCK-DIFF Q1–Q4; REVIEWS law approval; acceptance still needs user go-ahead
